subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should #94032 be resolved by the diagnostic-only PR #94045, or should OpenClaw pursue a broader exec private-LAN reachability or policy change?
rationale: The source-proven missing diagnostic is narrow, but making exec private-LAN access match other same-user contexts changes the security/runtime boundary and cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Land diagnostic-only fix
options.body: Treat #94045 as the immediate fix for the misleading operator experience and leave access policy unchanged while broader private-network issues remain tracked separately.

options.title: Design reachability parity
options.body: Keep #94032 open as a security design item until maintainers define when gateway exec may reach private networks and how that is surfaced to users.

options.title: Close as external runtime behavior
options.body: If maintainers decide the mismatch belongs entirely to Codex, macOS sandboxing, VPN, or Tailscale policy, close with that boundary and point users to the supported diagnostic/workaround path.

recommendation.title: Land diagnostic-only fix
recommendation.body: Treat #94045 as the immediate fix for the misleading operator experience and leave access policy unchanged while broader private-network issues remain tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to exec outcome and gateway/exec adjacent work, making them the best routing owner for the product/security choice.
